Modalidad: Online Apply online: Pay the US$ 30.00 application fee , according to the applicable Consular Fee Schedule . Register as a user: Go to the Integrated Migration Administration System (e-SAMI) and select “Registrar usuario” (Register User). Enter the requested information. You will receive a verification code by email. Enter the code on the platform to verify your account. Log in to the platform: Once your email address has been verified, you will receive your username and temporary password . Log in using these credentials, change your temporary password, and then log in again using your new password. Register your visa application: Select “New Application” and complete the required information in each section of the form. Upload the required documents, including an image of the proof of payment of the consular fee. The “Application Guide” will show you any mandatory fields that are still pending. Save and submit your application: Once you have completed all sections, select “Save Application”. If any information is still missing, your application will remain in “Draft” status so you can complete it later. Once all mandatory fields have been completed, its status will change to “Submitted” and it will be sent to the Consular Office. Wait for a response: The Consular Office will review the information and documentation submitted. The result of the evaluation and instructions on the next steps will be sent to the email address you registered on the platform . Do you need help with the application process? To learn how to complete your application step by step , we recommend reviewing the User Manual , where you will find instructions on how to register and correctly complete your online visa application. Submit your application Learn more about the procedures and services of the Consulate General of Peru in Chicago . Important Important: Payment gives you the right to submit an application and does not guarantee its approval. The payment is non-refundable, even if the visa application is denied. Submitting the application and required documentation does not guarantee visa issuance. Each application is evaluated individually by the Consul of Peru, who may request a personal interview or additional documentation if deemed necessary. There shall be no restrictions on OCI cardholders travelling to/from India during the period between issuance of a new passport and the final acknowledgment of the updated documents in the online system. However, OCI cardholders are advised to carry both their old and new passports while travelling to India on the basis of their OCI cards to facilitate smooth immigration/passport control procedures. Berlin Thursday, ***** × NOTICE 1. It has been decided to discontinue services of the authorized Outsourcing Service Provider, Alankit Assignments Ltd. w.e.f. 19.01.2026. 2. Accordingly, Indian Consular Application Centre (ICAC) operated by Alankit Assignments Ltd., located at “Sud Tower, 10th Floor, Eichhornstraße 3, 10785 Berlin” will NOT accept any applications (in person as well as postal) after 19.01.2026. 3. All the applications for Passport, Visa, OCI, Surrender Certificate, Attestation and other Miscellaneous Services will be accepted directly by the Embassy of India, Berlin located at Tiergartenstraße 17, 10785 Berlin, Germany from 20.01.2026 onwards through Online Appointment only. Check the relevant consular service details at Consular Services and accordingly book the appointment as directed. 4. Applicants must also ensure that they shall NOT transfer any fees to Alankit Assignment Ltd., for which services to be sought after 19.01.2026. The Embassy of India, Berlin will not be responsible for any such money transfers to Alankit Assignment Ltd. × Safety Advisory Several incidents have occurred in the last few years, as well as in last few months; where Indian nationals have drowned, while attempting to swim in lakes and rivers in Germany. It may kindly be noted that such activities should not be undertaken, except by expert swimmers who are familiar with the currents, depth and other threat parameters of water bodies in Germany. It is further advised that due precautions may be taken, such as wearing life jackets and all advisories of local governments on the matter should be strictly followed. × Advisory for International Passengers All the International passengers arriving in India are required to fill the Air Suvidha Self Declaration Form (SDF) by using Air Suvidha 2.0 portal prior to boarding the flight. SDF can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival to India. Passengers are requested to fill the forms before boarding of the flight, during web check-in for swift clearance on arrival and only required to show the downloaded SDF at the International Travel Health Desk or Immigration counter. All International travellers are requested to complete their Self-Declaration accurately and in advance, in the interest of passenger safety and Public Health. The portal may be accessed at https://airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in/ × Advisory on Fraud Calls Beware of fraudulent calls and messages claiming to be from the Embassy of India, Berlin or any other Indian authorities. The fraudsters claim to be officials of the Embassy of India, Berlin/Indian Consulates in Frankfurt, Hamburg and Munich. Apart from misguiding people with claims of wrong immigration data entry, etc they are demanding money. The Embassy or Consulates never ask for payments and sensitive information over Phone Calls. Do NOT share your personal details with anyone or make any payment over phone or email. Such fraud contacts should be reported to the Embassy immediately by sending an email to ca[dot]berlin[at]mea[dot]gov[dot]in and cons[dot]berlin[at]mea[dot]gov[dot]in . IMPORTANT NOTICE Government of India has decided to cancel, with immediate effect, all categories of existing physical visas issued earlier to Afghan nationals. Afghanistan Nationals may apply online for e-visa on New AFGHAN Portal: https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/avisa Afghanistan Nationals may avail following E-visa services: Business Visa, Student Visa, Medical Visa, Medical Attendant Visa, Entry Visa or UN Diplomat Visa INSTRUCTIONS Those travelling to India are also advised to go through instructions available on the website of the Bureau of Immigration at https://boi.gov.in . Each online application form is meant for one person only. A separate application has to be filed for each applicant. Furnish information exactly in the manner asked for in the forms, especially the names, passport number, address and date of birth. Applicants are required to verify the application details before submitting the online application. They have an option to save the online application form, in case it is not to be submitted. Once the online application form is submitted by the applicant, further modifications are not allowed. Hence, applicants are requested to check and validate the details before submitting the online application form. For any clarifications, Support Email id: indianvisaonline-boi@mha.gov.in Helpdesk: (+91) 82 7808 7808 Note: E-visa is directly dealt by New Delhi, Embassy/Consulates not responsible for E-visa E-visa : General guidelines For complete information of the e-Visa process, visit the official website https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/tvoa.html . e-Visas are not processed or issued / managed by the Embassy/Consulates in Germany. Do not use any other website, as the e Visa should be applied only through the authorized Indian Government website ( https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/ ). Ensure that the applicant provides correct particulars when filling up the online e-Visa application. e-Visa will carry particulars as provided by the applicant. In case particulars like the name and passport number are incorrectly filled up and e-Visa issued, the Embassy/Consulate cannot correct the particulars. The applicant has to apply again with correct particulars and obtain a new e-Visa. (Note: please check before final submission of your application online to avoid rejection or errors) In case of clarifications, visa applicant may contact the e-Visa Helpdesk at phone number 00-91-11-24300666 or email at indian-evisa@gov.in or indiatvoa@gov.in E-visa is directly dealt by New Delhi, Embassy/Consulates not responsible for E-visa. If the applicant is a Bangladeshi origin national living in United Kingdon or Ireland having required documents to prove his/her Bangladeshi origin. If the applicant is a Newborn of a Bangladeshi origin. If the applicant has an Existing MRP which has a validity less than 1 Year. We will not be able to receive any E-Passport application if the existing MRP has a validity more than one year. If the applicant has an E-Passport which has a validity of less than 1 year. If the applicant has an old styled Handwritten Bangladeshi passport. If the applicant lost the previous handwritten passport/MRP/E-Passport but has a copy of it. In that case a lost report reference letter lodged in the UK police department will be mandatory. The applicants must have a Bangladeshi National Id card (NID) or a 17 digit online verifiable Birth Registration Certificate (English Version) to apply for an E- Passport. If the application is with a Birth Registration Certificate, the BRC must be online verifiable and must contain English data. Please verify this from https://everify.bdris.gov.bd/ We will not be able to process an E-Passport application with a Birth Certificate which is issued from Dhaka South City Corporation after 2022. Note: Please check the document requirement section to check the eligibility. Click here . Mandatory Physical Appearance Please note that Physical Appearance is mandatory for e-passport enrolment, as such, applicants must take an appointment. While you apply, the appointments will be available towards the end of the application. All the applicants regardless of any age including Child and new-born must visit the High Commission on the date of passport application submission. Application Process: Steps of e-Passport application process Step 1: Applicants must lodge their application online. Please apply online at https://epassport.gov.bd/landing . Step 2: Appointment Booking: Applicants must make an appointment before visiting the High Commission. The appointment can be booked from the same portal after you have submitted the application. Step 3: Biometric Enrolment Applicants are required to appear in person on the date and time of appointment at the High Commission to submit their fingerprint, iris scan and signature. Although children under 6 years of age will be exempted from biometrics but under 6 children including new-born must visit the High Commission on the date of passport application submission with a 3R: 89 × 127 mm (3.5 in × 5 in) size lab printed photo. Step 4: Payment: The online payment option is not applicable for Bangladeshi mission abroad. On the day of the appointment Payments should be made using a credit card/Debit Card at the E-Passport counter. We will not accept any cash or postal order payment at the counter. Step 5: After the payment is made the applicants biometric (Fingerprints, Iris) will be captured and documents will be scanned, and the applicant will be handed over an enrolment slip. Step 6: Ready and Collection: Once the application is completed the applicant will be handed over an enrolment slip which will be required during passport collection. Email Notification will be sent to the applicant once the passport is ready for collection. The collection time will be from 11.00 AM to 12.30 PM and from 2.00 PM to 4.30 PM any working day after you get the email notification or see the tracking status as ‘Your passport is ready for issuance’ Tracking the Application Applicants can track the status of their application by visiting https://epassport.gov.bd/authorization/application-status Instruction regarding Filling in the form: Applicants must lodge their applications online. Please apply online via https://epassport.gov.bd/landing . Note: The applicants must use google chrome to open this link. The applicant will require an active email ID to create an account. During the online application process, ensure you have your NID or 17-digit online verifiable birth certificate (in English) at hand. Select ‘United Kingdom’ as your application processing office and then select London. When you fill in the application form, please make sure you are applying from United Kingdom and the Bangladesh Mission will be London. Please put your Permanent address in Bangladesh and present address in United Kingdom/Ireland. We will not be able to receive any application which is applied anywhere other than London. The application will not proceed if there is in any mistake in Permanent address and Present Address. After submitting your application, download the form and the summary sheet with the barcode (PDF format). After downloading, please print the form and summary sheet with appointment schedule. To apply for e-passport, you must have either a Bangladeshi NID card or a Birth Registration Certificate (BRC) (a 17-digit signed Birth Registration certificate which is verifiable at https://everify.bdris.gov.bd/ ). In case of BRC, please make sure that verified BRC contains the necessary data, e.g. names of the applicant, Date of Birth and the parents in English and they match with the corresponding data in your application. If they do not match, please contact the office from which the BRC was issued to do the necessary correction. Your passport application may be unsuccessful if there is a mismatch between your application, previous MRP/E-Passport/Hand written passport and NID or Birth Registration Certificate data. All data should match together in order for a successful E-Passport application. Avoid using prefixes like Mr./Mrs./Ms./Dr. with your first name. Instead, write your middle name (if any) with your first name, unless your existing documents specify otherwise. All fields marked with an asterisk (*) are mandatory. Do not deviate from the information provided in your NID/BRC. Machine-Readable Passports (MRPs) may still be used as long as they are valid, so there’s no need to apply for an e-Passport if your MRP’s validity extends beyond 1 year. If any discrepancies arise between your NID and MRP or BRC and MRP, they must be corrected before proceeding with your e-Passport application. Appointment Booking: Appointment booking for Biometric enrolment is a part of the successful application submission process. Appointments will be available towards the last part of the application. An applicant must secure an appointment to successfully submit the application. There may be no appointment available on the current month when the application is lodged due to huge demand from of e-Passports. The applicant should search in the next months to get available appointment dates. Offline Payment: After selecting appointment date and time, please check that on the bottom of the page there is a ‘Offline Payment’ text which will be ‘Non-functional/Greyed Out’. This means that for London mission no online payment is available, therefore the applicant needs to pay in the counter from their Bank Cards. Applicants need to go past this page and on the next page applicants will see a ‘Continue’ button on the bottom. The applicant must need to click this ‘Continue’ button. After hitting the ‘Continue’ button the application will be finally submitted. Then on the next page applicant needs to click on their name where they will see the full application to download and application summary sheet. On the day of the appointment, the applicants are required to bring these two documents along with other supporting documents. After selecting an appointment if the applicant does not Continue to next pages, the application will freeze here and the application will not be successfully submitted on the e-PP system. This will result an unsuccessful application submission even if an appointment was secured. For detail step by step guideline to fill in the E-Passport online application please click here . Required Documents Category 1: E-Passport Application from Bangladeshi Machine-Readable Passport (MRP)/E-Passport: Apply from https://epassport.gov.bd/landing Appointment Booking: : Applicants must make an appointment before visiting the High Commission. The appointment can be booked from the same portal after you have submitted the application. On the date of appointment, the applicant needs to bring the following documents: 1. Original Bangladeshi National ID card (NID)/Original of 17-digit signed Bangladeshi Birth Registration Certificate [English version will be required]. For Birth Certificate please make sure this is online verifiable from https://everify.bdris.gov.bd/ and English data is available. Please bring both the signed original Birth Registration Certificate and the verified copy. If the applicant does not have a Bangladeshi Birth Certificate, the BRC application can be made from this link: https://bhclondon.org.uk/birth-registration . 2. If your MRP/EPP was made with National ID Card (NID), the applicant must bring NID. You need to check the Personal Number Field of your passport to make sure whether the passport was made with NID or BRC. 3. Print the online completed form with barcode and the summary sheet with appointment. Please apply online via https://epassport.gov.bd/landing . 4. The applicant must bring the Existing original MRP/E-Passport. If the applicant lost his previous MRP/E-Passport, in that case, the applicant must bring a photocopy of the MRP/E-Passport and a lost report reference letter lodged in the UK police department will be mandatory. 5. Proof of Address of the Applicant. 6. If your marital status is changed from your previous MRP you must bring your Marriage Certificate/Divorce Certificate. If the marriage was conducted in the UK/Ireland, a Registered Marriage Certificate will be required. We do not accept Muslim Marriage Certificate. Any divorce must be solemnised by the court if the divorce was conducted in the UK. 7. If the applicant is a British/Irish/Any other country passport holder, the original British/Irish /Any other country passport will be necessary. 8. If the applicant is a full-time student and wants student discount fee the applicant must provide a Student ID card/School-University letter/CAS Letter where the enrolment starts, and end date is clearly mentioned. A primary/secondary school students also need to provide Studentship evidence in a paper format. This may include school letter/result sheet where students name is clearly mentioned. Please check this link for our Student discount policy . 9. Presence of the applicant during the enrolment is mandatory regardless of age. Category 2: For First Bangladesh Passport (Newborn of Bangladeshi origin/Bangladeshi origin of any age born in the UK and never had a Bangladeshi passport) Apply from https://epassport.gov.bd/landing Appointment Booking: Applicants must make an appointment before visiting the High Commission. The appointment can be booked from the same portal after you have submitted the application. On the date of appointment, the applicant needs to bring the following documents: 1. Original Bangladeshi National ID card (NID)/Original of 17-digit signed Bangladeshi Birth Registration Certificate [English version will be required]. For Birth Certificate please make sure this is online verifiable from https://everify.bdris.gov.bd/ and English data is available. Please bring both the signed original Birth Registration Certificate and the verified copy. If the applicant does not have a Bangladeshi Birth Certificate, the BRC application can be made from this link: https://bhclondon.org.uk/birth-registration . 2. Print the online completed form with barcode and the summary sheet. Please apply online via https://epassport.gov.bd/landing . 3. Original UK/Irish Birth Certificate/Any other country Birth Certificate [if the applicant is born in the UK or Ireland or any other country] 4. 3R: 89 × 127 mm (3.5 in × 5 in) size lab printed white background photo for the applicant up to 6 years of age. [The photo should not be older than 3 months] (2 copies). The child should wear a colourful dress. The background of the photo must be white and the background should be cover at least 40% area of the whole photo. Both the ear of the child should be visible. 5. Parents’ original MRP / Parents’ Old styled handwritten Bangladeshi passport/ Parents’ e-Passport / Parents’ Bangladeshi National ID card (NID) is mandatory. 6. Proof of Address will be required. 7. If the applicant is married and wants to include spouses name in the passport, the applicant must bring the registered Marriage Certificate. 8. For the adult applicant (Over 18 Years of age) who never had a Bangladeshi passport need to provide a basic DBS check from the UK authority. 9. If the applicant is a British/Irish/Any other country passport holder, the original British/Irish /Any other country passport will be necessary. 10. If the applicant is a full-time student and wants student discount fee the applicant must provide a Student ID card/School-University letter/CAS Letter where the enrolment starts, and end date is clearly mentioned. A primary/secondary school students also need to provide Studentship evidence in a paper format. This may include school letter/result sheet where students name is clearly mentioned. Please check this link for our Student discount policy . 11. Presence of the applicant during the enrolment is mandatory regardless of age. Category 3: E-Passport Application from Bangladeshi Handwritten Passport Apply from https://epassport.gov.bd/landing Appointment Booking: : Applicants must make an appointment before visiting the High Commission. The appointment can be booked from the same portal after you have submitted the application. On the date of appointment, the applicant needs to bring the following documents: 1. Original Bangladeshi National ID card (NID)/Original of 17-digit signed Bangladeshi Birth Registration Certificate [English version will be required]. For Birth Certificate please make sure this is online verifiable from https://everify.bdris.gov.bd/ and English data is available. Please bring both the signed original Birth Registration Certificate and the verified copy. If the applicant does not have a Bangladeshi Birth Certificate, the BRC application can be made from this link: https://bhclondon.org.uk/birth-registration . 2. Print the online completed form with barcode and the summary sheet. Please apply online via https://epassport.gov.bd/landing . 3. Original of Old styled handwritten Bangladeshi passport will be required. If the applicant lost his previous Handwritten passport, in that case, the applicant must bring a copy of the previous handwritten passport and a lost report reference letter lodged in the UK police department will be mandatory. 4. Proof of Address of the Applicant. 5. If the applicant is married and wants to include spouses name in the passport, the applicant must bring the Marriage Certificate. 6. If the applicant is a British/Irish passport holder, the Original of British/Irish passport will be necessary. 7. If the applicant is a full-time student and wants student discount fee the applicant must provide a Student ID card/School-University letter/CAS Letter where the enrolment starts, and end date is clearly mentioned. A primary/secondary school students also need to provide Studentship evidence in a paper format. This may include school letter/result sheet where students name is clearly mentioned. Please check this link for our Student discount policy . 8. Presence of the applicant during the enrolment is mandatory regardless of age. E-Passport documents checklist on the day of your appointment at the Bangladesh High Commission, London. click here . Data Correction from Previous Passport 1. If the applicant is over 18 years of age and wants any correction in the applicants Name, Parents name, Date of Birth and place of Birth from the applicants previous MRP/EPP/Handwritten passport, as per the instructions of the Bangladesh Ministry of Home Affairs the applicant must have a Bangladeshi National ID card which will support these corrections. For the applicants who are over 18 years, we will not be able to receive any correction application based on the corrected Digital Birth Certificate. If the applicant is under 18 years of age the above correction applications will be accepted based on Digital Birth Certificate. However, these corrections are subject to the approval of the Department of immigration and Passport office Dhaka and may need a prior Police verification. Hence, the estimated processing time may be more than usual. 2. If an applicant wants to add or remove his/her spouse’s name in ePassport, then he/she must bring their registered marriage certificate or divorce certificate (Decree of Absolute/solemnised by the court) or both (removal of previous spouse name and adding new one). 3. The applicant may correct or change the emergency contact address, in that case the applicant must provide one utility bills of the emergency contact address. Very Important Instructions Before applying to avoid common mistakes 1. The application must be submitted to Bangladesh High Commission London. Please ensure you selected ‘NO’ when it asks for ‘Are you applying from Bangladesh’ and then select ‘United Kingdom/Ireland’ as your country and then select ‘London’ as your Bangladeshi mission. When the system asks for Present address, please select UK/Ireland as your present address. If you provide your present address in Bangladesh by mistake, your application will be submitted in Bangladesh. THE HIGH COMMISSION, LONDON WILL NOT BE ABLE TO RECEIVE ANY APPLICATION WHICH IS SUBMITTED IN ANY PASSPORT OFFICE IN BANGLADESH INSTEAD OF LONDON OFFICE. In that case the application must individually contact the passport office in Bangladesh and will need to cancel the application to resubmit in London. 2. If you have a previous Machine-readable passport or an E-Passport, you must select the appropriate box. If you have a handwritten passport, you must select ‘No I do not have/Handwritten passport’ box. 3. Before appearing the High Commission on the date of your appointment, please make sure your Birth Certificate/NID has the same data and spelling (specially Name, date of Birth, Place of Birth and parents name) as per your previous MRP/E-Passport/Handwritten passport. For a very small mismatch in data among Application, MRP/E-Passport with BRC/NID; the application may not be successful or may get delayed in Bangladesh. The High Commission will not be responsible for such delay or for unsuccessful application. The 17 Digit Birth Registration data must be online verifiable and need to make sure that the ENGLISH version data is available in database. The 17digit Birth Registration data can be verified from https://everify.bdris.gov.bd/ this link. 4. For applying a new Passport having a previous Bangladeshi passport is mandatory (this is exempted for the UK born only). If you are staying in UK for a long time and have lost your previous Bangladeshi Handwritten passport and you do not have at last a copy of your handwritten passport in that case Parents Bangladeshi Passport/NID, Bangladesh local chairman Nationality Certificate and Succession Certificate may be required. These applications must be supported by a Lost Police Report. However, additional documents may be required based on the interview for the passport application. The application will not be accepted if you appear only with the application and with a digital Birth Certificate. Other General Instructions: As per the recent changes, spouses name does not appear on the physical E-passport. The spouse name is only included in the database. If an applicant wants to add or remove his/her spouse’s name in ePassport database, then he/she must bring their registered marriage certificate or divorce certificate (Decree of Absolute/solemnised by the court) or both of these (removal of previous spouse name and adding new one). If someone loose his/her e-Passport and wants to make a new e-Passport, he must bring a lost report from police. Light colour dresses (such ash white, sky, ash etc.) may cause photo capturing refusal engraved in system software. Applications are cordially requested to avoid light-coloured dresses. If case of biometric capturing difficulties i.e medical lenses, finger amputation or skin problems that may demand the biometric exemption, valid and specific letter from concern Physician/NHS/GP must be shown at the time of enrolment. We will not be able to process an E-Passport application with a Birth Certificate issued from Dhaka South City Corporation after 2022. Any changes to the information provided, or undisclosed/fraudulent information, may result in potential cancellation/ delays/ extending the usual processing time. A passport application may also be cancelled if any undeclared MRP/E-Passport is found after fingerprint capture. e-Passport Fee and Mode of Payment and processing time: Offline Payment: After selecting appointment date and time, please check that on the bottom of the page there is a ‘Offline Payment’ text which will be ‘Non-functional/Greyed Out’. This means that for London mission no online payment is available, therefore the applicant needs to pay in the counter from their Bank Cards. On the date of your appointment the e-Passport fee will be taken from the counter from the applicants Bank card. The applicants are requested to keep sufficient fund for paying the fees. The High Commission does not accept any cash payment. Please do not pay in A-Challan or e-Challan. A-Challan or e-Challan is only accepted exclusively for passport office who applies in Bangladesh. After successful application submission the applicant will see E-passport fee in the application in Dollar currency. However, the actual fee that needs to be paid in the counter will be in British pound Currency. The E-Passport fee for Bangladesh High Commission London is calculated in British Pounds and is fixed considering the Dollar to Pound currency conversion fluctuation. Passport Fees Type of Applicant Passport Pages Passport Duration Regular Express General Applicants 48 Page 5 Years 96 Pound 145 Pound 10 Years 118 Pound 170 Pound 64 Page 5 Years 145 Pound 195 Pound 10 Years 167 Pound 220 Pound Students 48 Page 5 Years 30 Pound 45 Pound 10 Years 50 Pound 75 Pound 64 Page 5 Years 145 Pound 195 Pound 10 Years 167 Pound 220 Pound Note: On the application form, the fee given will be in US Dollar currency. The above fees in Pounds are calculated based on the dollar-to-pound conversion calculation. Note: Express delivery will only be possible if the applicant has a previous MRP or an E-Passport (date of issue is within last 10 years) and there is no data mismatch between Application, previous MRP/E-Passport and Birth Registration Certificate/NID. Express delivery will not be successful if there is any Police Verification is required in Bangladesh in the application process. Student Discount Policy Full-time students are eligible for discounted fees. To qualify, you must provide valid proof of studentship that clearly states your enrolment start and end dates. Acceptable documents include: School, college, or university letter Student ID card CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies) letter ZIP card (as proof of student status) Please note: Proof of studentship is required regardless of age if you wish to receive a student discount. A primary/High School student should also bring the studentship proof. Part-time and ESOL students are not eligible for student discounts. Students enrolled in PhD, Post-Doctoral, or MPhil programs are not eligible for discounted fees. A full fee will be charged if acceptable documentation is not provided in paper format. Passport fees are non-refundable regardless of whether the application is rejected or withdrawn. The High Commission accepts only the Credit/Debit card payable in the counter. We do not accept any cash payment. Processing time: The processing time for an e-Passport may vary due to the thorough security and information validation procedures implemented by both the e-Passport system, Department of Immigration and Passport office, Dhaka. Regular Delivery If there is no mismatch of data between Application, MRP/EPP and between NID/BRC we expect to deliver the passport within 4 to 6 weeks’ time. Express Delivery If there is no police verification required and if there is no mismatch of data between Application, MRP/EPP and between NID/BRC we expect to deliver the passport within 21 days’ time. Note: The above time is not always guaranteed as the whole process depends on the process of Bangladesh Immigration and Passport authority. Tracking the Application Applicants can track the status of their application by visiting https://epassport.gov.bd/authorization/application-status Collecting the passport You will get an email notification on the email address that you used to create the user ID when the passport is ready for issuance. The collection time will be from 11.00 AM to 12.30 PM and from 2.00 PM to 4.30 PM any working day after you get the email notification or see the tracking status as ‘Your passport is ready for issuance’. Applicants need to bring the original delivery slip for collecting the passports. Only in the case of medical emergency an E-Passport can be collected by an authorized person. In that case the authorized person must bring his/her Bangladeshi passport/NID/BRC and signed AUTHORIZATION LETTER from the applicant. The format of AUTHORIZATION LETTER is available here: https://bhclondon.org.uk/forms-to-download Parents must collect the passport of a child. Parents must bring the original delivery receipt and Parents Bangladeshi passport/NID/BRC. What will happen on the day of your appointment: After arriving at the High Commission, the applicant needs to go to the 27 Queens gate from where the applicant needs to collect a token. Tokens will be given as per the appointment schedule. When you have the token, you need to come to the 28 Queens gate basement consular area counter 1. Your documents will be checked in the counter and payment will be taken. After the payment you need to wait for the biometric capture. When the biometric is completed, you will be handed over a delivery receipt and collection instructions. The whole process might need approximately 1 hour to complete. So, you are requested to keep enough time in your hand. We will try to serve you as per your given appointment schedule and time. However, as we deal with quite a large number of applicants this might not always possible due to the pre-existing queue, difficulties in previous applicants’ biometric capture and documents checking. Any Bangladeshi Origin British/EU National with valid resident permit in UK who has a Bangladeshi Passport/ Bangladeshi national ID card (NID)/ Bangladeshi Birth certificate can apply for NVR. - Spouse and Children of a Bangladeshi origin British/EU National can also apply for NVR subject to providing sufficient documents. - The fee is 70 Pounds. - Delivery time for in-person application is 5-7 working days and for postal the time is 21 days. - In person applications are appointment only. - NVR is never an urgent service. Documents Required for No Visa Required (NVR) Documents are required based on the following categories: 1. NVR for Who has a Bangladeshi passport or a Birth Certificate: Duly filled in online application form available at https://visa.gov.bd . A Photocopy of Bangladeshi passport or a Bangladeshi Birth Certificate or a National ID card. You must bring the original copy during in person submission. A passport size photograph attached with the filled in online application form (glued not stapled) 2. NVR for Who’s Spouse has a Bangladeshi document. Duly filled in online application form available at https:/visa.gov.bd . A Photocopy of Bangladeshi passport or a national ID Card (NID) or a Bangladeshi Birth Certificate of the spouse. The registered marriage certificate/Nikah Nama. If the marriage was conducted in the UK the council registered marriage certificate will be required. A declaration of marriage needs to be provided on the day of the application submission. The format of declaration is given here . A passport size photograph attached with the filled in online application form (glued not stapled) The applicant and the Bangladeshi spouse must be present at the High Commission on the day of appointment for interview. Note:Husbands or Wife’s NVR will not qualify the spouse for a NVR. Husband or the wife must have a Bangladeshi Passport/NID/ Bangladeshi Birth Certificate. 3. NVR for Who’s parent has a Bangladeshi document. Note: Parents NVR will not qualify the children for an NVR. Any parent must have a Bangladeshi Passport/NID/Bangladeshi Birth Certificate. Duly filled in online application form available at https:/visa.gov.bd . A Photocopy of Bangladeshi passport or a National ID Card (NID) or a Bangladeshi Birth Certificate of the parent. The Birth Certificate of the child where parents name is clearly mentioned. A passport size photograph attached with the filled in online application form (glued not stapled) Online application guideline for No Visa Required (NVR) Do not use MAC pc to fill up the form. Please DO NOT USE any special characters while filling out the address filed (such as , ; ' : - _ etc.). Please skip payment option while filling up online application. Please skip photo upload. Please select ‘Others’ in the organizations field and write ‘others’ or ‘none’ in the box which will appear at the right-hand side. No Visa Required (NVR) submission NVR can be applied either of the following two ways: Physical Presence at the High Commission with a prior appointment. By using Postal Service For APPOINTMENTS, please ensure the following steps: Submission of the online Form on https:/visa.gov.bd ; Take a print-out of the PDF version of the submitted application file. Proceed to the next step to confirm booking of appointment online from https://bhclondon.org.uk/no-visa-appointment ; and Arrive and avail service on the date of the appointment at the BHC London Office. Please bring all the documents as mentioned in the document requirement section. POSTAL APPLICATION GUIDELINES: In case of NVR APPLICATION by POST, please follow the step by step guidelines as given below: Note: We suggest you post this with the Royal mail tracking service. And please keep this tracking reference number with you for future query. A) Please fill-in the online form on https:/visa.gov.bd ; B) Take a print of the filled-in Form C) Enclose your original British/Irish Passport with the documents states in the document requirement section. D) Go to a nearby post office (Royal Mail); E) Collect a postal order of £70.00 in favor of ''Bangladesh High Commission, London'' and enclose that postal with your application form; F) Collect a self-addressed return postal envelop. The envelope should be Next Day Recorded Delivery prepaid envelope (up to two passport we require 100-gram prepaid envelope, up to five passport we require 500-gram prepaid envelope). Photo Capture Instructions: Please click a new photo using your mobile device (with the flashlight turned off) that meets the following specifications: • Taken from a distance of at least 1.5 meters. • Wear dark clothes. • Use a light-colored background • Ensure no shadows on the face or background. • Eyes open and clearly visible. • Do not use filters or photo editing tools. • Maintain a natural expression (no smiling or frowning). • Ensure even lighting across the face. • No red-eye effect. • Image resolution should be higher than 2500 x 2500 pixels. • Forehead visible – no hair, cap, hijab, or turban covering it. • Head straight, not tilted. • Ears must be visible. • If wearing a turban, it must be light in color (white or light blue). 2. Open the picture Using MS Paint 3. You can change the background color to white if the photo does not have white background. 4. Cropping Instructions: • Crop the picture by dragging inward from all four sides. • The space between the ears and the edge of the picture should not be more than what is shown in the sample image below. • The free space above the head should also not exceed the example shown. • Your face should cover approximately 80% of the photo area. 5. Now, resize the picture to 630 x 810 pixels using MS Paint. Make sure to turn off the “Maintain aspect ratio” option before changing the pixel dimensions. • • • The image size must be exactly 630 x 810 pixels and less than 250 KB. Save the image in JPEG format. If the file size is over 250 KB, please open the image and resize it to reduce the size before uploading. No action is required; simply open this file and click Save. Scan and crop the signature into a rectangular shape (not exceeding 100 KB) and upload it. Do not upload the entire page. SBIePay is the Payment Aggregator service of State Bank of India, India's Largest Bank and amongst top 50 Banks in the world, which provides bouquet of multiple payment options on a single page for the convenience of the customers. 2. What are the payment channels available for e-Visa? SBIePay has facilitated the following channels on e-Visa platform: Payment Gateway: It seamlessly processes Credit card and Debit Card transactions for all the cards issued internationally by Visa & MasterCard. SBIePay Payment gateway is enabled with BIN identifier which recognises the BIN online when a customer enters the no., which drastically improves the success percentage and reduces customer friction. Paypal: SBIePay also facilitates e-Visa customers to make payment through widely popular and accepted Paypal channel. 3. Are transactions on SBIePay secure? SBIePay is certified with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) ver 3.2, which is the latest version, and which further reinforces our promise of security and safety. The payment system fully supports 3DSecure - Verified by Visa and MasterCard Secure Code, wherever it is applicable. Further, SBIePay is secured using Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) encryption which ensures that payment information that travels over the Internet is always encrypted and cannot be viewed by unauthorised individuals. 4. Can International payments be processed? Yes, SBIePay has enabled international card issued by MasterCard and VISA both with and without 3D Secure authentication. 5. How a customer/applicant can understand that payment has been made successfully? The applicant enters necessary details on https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/ , and clicks on 'Pay Now'. The applicant is redirected to SBIePay payment page and is presented with payment options of either entering Card details (Payment Gateway) or Paypal .Applicant enters his card details and clicks "Proceed". Now, either of the below mentioned 2 scenarios will occur: 3 D Secure page of the Card Issuerwill be displayed, where applicant must enter 3D Secure Password/OTP. Transaction is processed without 3D Secure page. After successful completion of transaction, the applicant is redirected on to the https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/ with a successful receipt of payment. 6. How do I know that my Bank participates in 3D Secure transaction? If an applicant is presented with a 3D Secure page prompting to enter a password/OTP, this means the Card issuing Bank participates in 3D Secure transaction. If the applicant's transaction is processed without directing to 3D secure page, he/she should contact the card issuing Bank for support. 7. What if a successful page on https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/ is not shown after completing the transaction? In an ideal scenario, once the transaction is processed, the applicant shall be presented with a payment successful page along with a reference number. In some rare scenarios it may happen where the application is not shown Payment successful page post completion of transaction, which may be due to a drop in connectivity leading to non-receipt of success response. If the applicant does not receive any success message even after card account has been charged, a refund shall be initiated after due reconciliation process to the applicant's card account. 8. How are Refunds processed? In rare case of transaction status unknown to the applicant, which is when the applicant has not received success response due to time out or connectivity issue and the account has been debited, we advise the customer not to attempt another transaction immediately and rather provide their Order no. on the e-Visa site after 30 minutes to check the status of the transaction. If the transaction status is showing "failed", then customer may attempt another transaction. Also, the debited amount shall be refunded to the applicant's card account after reconciliation process within seven (7) days of transaction. 9. What are the banking charges for e-Visa fee? The banking charges for: Payment Gateway Card transactions (both Debit or Credit Card): 3%* of the applicable e-Visa fee. Paypal: 4%* of the applicable e-Visa fee. *The charges are inclusive of any applicable taxes. The breakup of transaction charges will be displayed on the Payment page for applicant's knowledge and to maintain transparency. 10. What is the support available for the applicants? At State Bank of India, we are committed to provide best customer services to our customers. Customers can email us at sbiepay[at]sbi[dot]co[dot]in for any queries related to their transaction. Alternatively, SBIePay provides 24*7*365 customer support to all the e-Visa applicants. Applicants can also call us on the below mentioned number(s): Contact No: +91-022-65361671 11. Can an applicant perform more than one transaction for same application number registered at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/ ? An applicant can perform multiple times transactions for a single application ID, with a gap of minimum 25 minutes between each transaction. It is advisable that applicant may check the status of the transaction at e-Visa portal before attempting another transaction. 12. Can https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/ charge more than one time for an application ID? An applicant shall be charged for only once for any successful transaction against an application ID. Any further debits shall be refunded back to the customer after due reconciliation, within seven (7) days of transactions. 1. What is Axis Bank Payment Gateway service? Axis Bank is an Internet Payment Gateway Solution allows you to make payments on a 24 X 7 basis from around the world. It accepts all Visa, MasterCard and Maestro cards. 2. What are the various payment modes available on Axis Bank payment gateway page? Axis Bank Payment Gateway services facilitates online payments w.r.t. all Credit and Debit Cards issued by MasterCard and VISA. 3. Are transactions on Axis Bank Payment Gateway secure? Axis Bank Payment gateway services is compliant with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) standards. All transactions initiated at Axis Bank Payment Gateway services come with 128 bit security and two factor authentication via MasterCard Secure Code and Verified-by-Visa authentication is enabled. 4. Can International payments be processed? Axis Bank Payment gateway accepts all international card issued by MasterCard and VISA both with and without 3D secure authentication. 5. How a customer/applicant can understand that payment has been made successfully? The applicant after filling details on https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/ clicks 'Pay Now'. The applicant is redirected to Axis Bank payment gateway page and is presented with payment options like MasterCard and VISA. Cardholder enters his card number, expiry date, Name and CVV value and clicks 'Pay Now'. Incase cardholder Bank is enabled for 3D secure, then a page will appear for the cardholder to entire either his/her OTP/3D secure password. Else transaction would be processed. After successful completion of transaction, the applicant is redirected on to the https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/ with a successful receipt of payment. 6. How do I know that my Bank participates in 3D Secure transaction? Incase Bank is participating for 3D Secure transaction during transaction a 3D secure page would appear and cardholders have to enter his/her password /OTP. 7. What if a successful page on https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/ is not shown after completing the transaction? The applicant shall be presented with a payment successful page along with reference number. If the applicant does not receive any success message even after card account has been charged, a refund will have to be initiated after due reconciliation to the applicant's card account. 8. How are Refunds processed? If a transaction has failed but the applicants card account is debited more than once, the amount will have to be refunded to the applicant's card account after reconciliation process within seven (7) days of transaction. In some cases, If the fund still lies with the card issuing Bank, kindly get in touch with your Bank for such case. 9. What are the banking charges for e-Visa fee? The banking charges are subject to maximum of 3% plus applicable taxes on the applicable e-Visa fees. These charges are charged to the applicant at the time of making online e visa fee payment. 10. What is the support available for the applicants ? Axis Bank provides technical support for all payment related transactions at ecom[at]axisbank[dot]com 11. What are the things that the cardholder needs to take care of before initiating the transaction? Our endeavour is to provide you with a seamless experience on our platform. Please ensure following, before initiating the card payment. Using a non-expired card Have sufficient balance in your account Have sufficient credit card limit on the card being used Card is not reported as 'lost or stolen' Entering the correct OTP. Have access to device for accessing OTP or Static password Card supports transactions in INR and USD Amount has not exceeded the daily maximum allowed amount by your issuer Number of transactions have not exceeded the daily maximum allowed count by your issuer Issuer and card not enrolled for 3DS Timeout occurred while receiving the OTP from issuer or while entering OTP on the payment page 1. What is Razorpay Payment Gateway service? Razorpay is a payment technology platform that enables secure online payment processing. Razorpay provides a range of payment options to facilitate convenient and seamless payment of e-Visa fees by applicants. 2. What are the various payment modes available on Razorpay payment gateway page? Razorpay facilitates online payments through supported international credit and debit cards, along with other payment methods like Apple Pay, Google Pay and Paypal. The available payment options will be displayed on the Razorpay payment page. 3. Are transactions on Razorpay Payment Gateway secure? Yes. Razorpay uses industry-standard security and authentication measures to protect payment transactions. Depending on the card issuer and transaction, applicants may be required to complete additional authentication such as OTP or 3D Secure authentication. 4. Can International payments be processed? Yes. Razorpay supports international card payments, subject to the card network, issuing bank, transaction eligibility and applicable regulatory and risk controls. 5. How a customer/applicant can understand that payment has been made successfully? After entering the required payment details and completing any applicable authentication, the transaction will be processed. Upon successful payment, the applicant will be redirected to the e-Visa portal and the payment status will be updated. Applicants are advised to wait for the payment confirmation before closing or refreshing the browser. 6. How do I know that my Bank participates in 3D Secure transaction? If your card issuer supports and requires 3D Secure authentication, you will be redirected to the relevant authentication page during the payment process. You may be required to enter an OTP, password or complete another authentication step as specified by your card-issuing bank. 7. What if a successful page on https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/ is not shown after completing the transaction? If your card/account has been charged but a successful payment confirmation is not displayed on the e-Visa portal, please do not immediately make another payment. Please check the payment status on the e-Visa portal. If the transaction remains unsuccessful or unresolved, it will be subject to reconciliation and the applicable refund process. 8. How are Refunds processed? If a transaction fails but the applicant's account is debited, the transaction will be reconciled. Where a refund is applicable, the amount will be refunded to the original payment method after completion of the reconciliation process. Refund timelines may vary depending on the applicant's card-issuing bank or payment provider. 9. What are the banking charges for e-Visa fee? Applicable payment processing charges, if any, will be displayed to the applicant on the payment checkout page before completing the transaction. The applicable charges may vary depending on the payment method and applicable e-Visa payment terms. 10. What is the support available for the applicants ? Razorpay Payment Support: Email : sng-service[at]razorpay[dot]com Contact number: 99626 5644 For queries related to the e-Visa application, visa processing or immigration, applicants should contact the relevant e-Visa/BoI support team. 11. What are the things that the cardholder needs to take care of before initiating the transaction? To ensure a seamless payment experience, please ensure the following before initiating the card payment: The card is valid and has not expired. Sufficient balance or credit limit is available. International transactions are enabled on the card, where applicable. The card has not been reported as lost or stolen. Correct card details are entered. The applicant has access to the registered device/email to receive OTPs, where applicable. The card supports the applicable transaction currency. The transaction amount is within the limits set by the card-issuing bank. The number of transactions is within the limits set by the card-issuing bank. Any required 3D Secure authentication is completed successfully. 12. Can an applicant perform more than one transaction for the same application number? An applicant may retry a payment if the previous transaction was unsuccessful. However, applicants are advised to check the payment status on the e-Visa portal before initiating another transaction to avoid duplicate payments. If a previous transaction is still pending, applicants should wait for the status to be updated before attempting another payment. Close FAQ's × Q1. Who is eligible for e-Visa Services? Ans- The following are the eligibility conditions for availing e-Visa services-   i. Nationals of countries listed on the e-Visa website https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/ are eligible to apply for e-Visa Services.   ii. Foreigners whose sole objective for visiting India is     (a) Recreation and sightseeing     (b) Casual visit to meet friends and relatives     (c) Attending short term yoga programme or short term courses on local languages, music, dance, arts & crafts, cooking, medicine etc. which should not be a formal or structured course/programme      (courses not exceeding 6 months duration and not issuing a qualifying certificate/diploma etc. to the participants)     (d) Voluntary work of short duration (for a maximum period of one month, which do not involve any monetary payment or consideration of any kind in return)     (e) Medical treatment, including treatment under Indian systems of medicine     (f) As attendant to e-Medical visa holder     (g) Business purpose     (h) Attending a conference/ seminar/ workshop.   iii. Passport should have at least six months validity at the time of making application for grant of e-Visa and a re-entry permit, if that is required under the law of the country of nationality of the applicant.    The passport should have at least two blank pages for stamping by the Immigration Officer.   iv. The foreigner should have return ticket or onward journey ticket, with sufficient money to spend during his/her stay in India.   v. Foreigners of Pakistani origin or having Pakistani Passport are not eligible for e-Visa. Foreigners who are not Pakistani nationals, but whose parents or grandparents (either paternal or maternal) was born    in, or was permanently resident in Pakistan, are also not eligible for e-Visa. They may apply for regular Visa at Indian Mission.   vi. Not available to Diplomatic/Official Passport Holders or Laissez-passer/ international travel document holders.   vii. Not available to individuals endorsed on Parent's/Spouse's Passport i.e. each individual should have a separate passport. Q2. What is the procedure of applying for e-Visa? Ans- For details regarding procedure for applying, please visit our website: https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/ Q3. Is there any other website apart from the government website to apply for the e-Visa application? Ans- No, https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/ is only the official website to apply for the e-Visa Services.    Note - Services of e-Visa are completely online and no facilitation is required by any intermediary / travel agents etc. It is advised not to believe or fall in trap of any such unscrupulous elements who claim    speedy/express grant of e-Visa and charge money for it.    Do not share your personal information with any unauthorized website as it may lead to leakage of your personal data. Only visit the official website https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/ for e-Visa    service.    For any clarification, you may write us on our email id ' indian-evisa[at]gov[dot]in ' or contact us on (+91) 827808 7808 or +91 11 24300666 . Q4. Is there any fee other than the processing fee? Ans- No, there is no fee other than the processing fee for e-Visa application and it is non-refundable. Please visit our website to know the fee applicable for your country as it is country-specific. Q5. When should I apply? Ans- (i) For e-Tourist Visa (01 year / 05 years), e-Business Visa, e-Medical, e-Medical Attendant and e-Conference visa, applicants of the eligible countries/territories may apply online minimum 4 days in advance    of the date of arrival. Such application can be made 120 days in advance from proposed date of travel.    (ii) For e-Tourist Visa (30 days) , applicants of the eligible countries/territories may apply online minimum 4 days in advance of the date of arrival. Such application can be made 120 days in advance from    proposed date of travel. Q6. Do I get a confirmation of submission of my e-Visa application? Ans- Yes. Immediately after you submit your e-Visa application and make the payment, you will receive a confirmation of submission of your application on the email id provided by you while filling up your    application form. Q7. When will my e-Visa be issued and how will I be informed about it? Ans- You will be intimated about your Visa status (Granted or Rejected) on your email id provided by you in the e-Visa application. Q8. Can I check the status of my e-Visa application? Ans- Yes, you may check the status of your e-Visa application by visiting our website: https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/ and clicking on 'Check your Visa Status' Tab provided on the website. Q9. What is the validity of e-Visa? Ans- The validity of e-Visa would be according to the e-Visa service you have requested in the application form as -    For e-Tourist Visa (01 year / 05 years) , the validity would be 365 days / 05 years from the date of grant of ETA with Multiple entries and Maximum stay in India during one Calender Year should not exceed 180 days.    For e-Tourist Visa (30 days) , the validity would be 30 days from the date of your first arrival in India. Multiple entries will be granted within the e-Visa validity period stamped on your Passport. Your first    arrival must be between the date of issue and expiry of ETA.    For e-Business Visa , the validity would be 365 days from the date of grant of ETA with Multiple entries and continuous stay during each visit which shall not exceed 180 days and no registration would be    required if stay is for a period of less than 180 days. However, if the intention is to stay for more than 180 days, then the foreigner shall get himself/herself registered with the FRRO/FRO concerned    (https://indianfrro.gov.in) within two weeks after the expiry of 180 days of his/her arrival in India.    For e-Conference Visa , the validity would be 30 days from the date of arrival in India with Multiple entry.    For e-Medical Visa , the validity would be 60 days from the date of first arrival in India and Multiple entry will be allowed within the e-Visa validity period stamped on your Passport.    For e-Medical Attendant Visa , the validity would be 60 days from the date of first arrival in India and Multiple entry will be allowed within the e-Visa validity period stamped on your Passport. Q10. Can I convert my e-Visa to any other Visa? Ans- No, e-Visa is non-extendable and non-convertible. Q11. Can I change the port of arrival/departure? Ans- You may arrive at 33 designated Airports i.e. Ahmedabad, Amritsar, Bagdogra, Bengaluru, Bhubaneshwar, Calicut, Chennai, Chandigarh, Cochin, Coimbatore, Delhi, Gaya, Goa(Dabolim), Goa(Mopa), Guwahati, Hyderabad, Indore, Jaipur, Kannur, Kolkata, Lucknow, Madurai, Mangalore, Mumbai, Nagpur, Port Blair, Pune, Surat, Tiruchirapalli, Trivandrum, Varanasi, Vijayawada & Vishakhapatnam, and 19 designated seaports (i.e. Agatti , Calicut , Chennai , Cochin , Goa , Kamarajar , Kandla , Kattupali , Kolkata , Kollam , Mangalore , Mumbai , Mundra , Nhava Sheva , Port Blair , Vallarpadam , Vishakhapatnam , Vizhinjam and Vizhinjam International). You may depart from any of the Indian Immigration Check Posts (ICPs). Q12. I am applying e-Visa for myself and my son/daughter who is a minor. Do I need to apply for a separate e-Visa for my minor child? Ans- Yes, ensure that your child's passport is valid at-least for next 06 (six) months from the date of arrival in India. Q13. I have submitted my e-Visa application and paid the processing fee. If I cancel my proposed visit to India, will the fees be refunded? Ans- e-Visa processing fee once submitted is non-refundable as the fee is for processing of the application and is not dependent on either Grant or Rejection of Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) Q14. Do I have to pay anything else at the airport for e-Visa (other than the processing fee paid by me online)? Ans- No. You have already paid the required processing fee online. The applicants are advised to beware of unscrupulous elements/ travel agents/ intermediaries demanding extra payment. Q15. I want to submit my liquor permit application along with my e-visa application how can I do this? Ans- This pertains to customs department. Q16. What should I do if the payment is not accepted by the e-Visa website? Ans- Make sure you delete the browser history and cookies before trying to make payment. Also try to change the browser if the problem persists.    In case you have already tried more than thrice, then you may have to re-submit the entire application form once again.    Payment Support helpline :-    Axis Bank Technical support. Email address: ecom[at]axisbank[dot]com    Contact No Toll free Numbers from:    USA : 18552055577 UK : 0808178 5040 Singapore : 8001206355 Australia : 1800153861 UAE : 8000 3570 3218 Saudi Arabia : 8008500000 Qatar : 00800 100348 Bahrain : 80011300    For rest of the countries: + 91-40-6717-4100    SBI ePay payment support provides technical support for all payment related transactions at +91-022-65361671 (24 x 7). Q17. How can I get the invoice/receipt of the e-Visa payment? Ans- Please visit our website https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/ and click on 'Verify Payment/ Pay e-Visa fee'. Q18. What are the necessary documents required to apply for an e-Business Visa other than the Passport? Ans - You have to upload the business card along with the details of Indian Firm/Company (which you intend to associate yourself with) for business activities. For Sports Related Activity under e-Business Visa, please refer Instructions for applicant page for the list of documents required. Q19. What is a Business Card? Ans- Business card means 'a card provided to you by the company you are working for' OR you can also upload 'an invitation letter from the company in India including company's information, address and    phone number in India'. Q20. What are the necessary documents required for e-Medical Visa other than the Passport? Ans - A Copy of Letter from the Hospital concerned in India on its letterhead which includes the tentative date of admission/treatment in the hospital mentioning the name, nationality and Passport number of    the patient/ e-Medical Visa applicant. Q21. What are the necessary documents required for e-Conference Visa other than the Passport? Ans- For e-Conference Visa, following are the required documents:    (i) Invitation from organizer (mandatory)    (ii) Political clearance from Ministry of External Affairs, Govt of India (mandatory)    (iii) Event clearance from Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt of India (optional) Q22. I got a new passport but my ETA was on old passport and it is still valid. How can I proceed now? Ans- You may be allowed entry into India on the new passport even if ETA has been issued on the old passport with the condition that you must carry the new Passport and old passport on which ETA was    issued. Q23. Can I enter India using Land border even if I am having valid e-visa for any other airport or seaport which is not listed for the e-Visa ? Ans- No, You can only enter through the designated airports/seaports which are listed on the e-Visa website. Q24. How can I fill previous Visa details inside the e-Visa application form? Ans- You have to put the Previous visa details in the application form as it is mandatory. You can write NA or Not Available or Not Applicable or any other suitable phrase according to you in the application    form if you do not remember your earlier Visa number/details. Q25. Can I get Visa on Arrival(VoA) at Indian Airports/Seaport? Ans- The Visa on Arrival facility is only for the nationals of Japan, South Korea and UAE (only for such UAE nationals who had earlier obtained e-Visa or regular/paper visa for India). For the nationals of all other    countries eligible for e-Visa, the e-visa application have to be filled online and the applicant must wait till the confirmation/Grant of ETA for travelling to India. Q26. Can I get a refund for the rejected e-Visa application? Ans- e-Visa processing fee once submitted is non-refundable as the fee is for processing of the application and is not dependent on either grant or Rejection of the Application. Q27. Can I use e-Visa to enter in India by cruise Ship? Ans- Entry by cruise ship is allowed with the ETA through 5 designated seaports namely Mumbai, Chennai, Cochin, Goa and Mangalore seaports. Q28. What is 'Visible Identification Mark'? Ans- 'Visible identification mark' generally means moles, birthmarks, permanent scars etc. which are visible and can be shown if askd for by the Indian Immigration Authority. Q29. Who have to carry the 'Yellow Fever Vaccination card'? Ans- All the foreigners arriving in India within 6 days of departure from any yellow fever endemic country are required to possess (in original) a valid yellow fever certificate of vaccination.    List of Yellow fever vaccination countries-    https://mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/Updated%20List%20of%20Yellow%20Fever%20Endemic%20Countries%20by%20WHO_0.pdf Q30. We got the ETA, but have discrepancy in the Name, Nationality, Passport Number and Date of Birth in the ETA ? Ans- The applicant must check all the details including Name, Nationality, Passport Number and Date of Birth, photograph/self image etc before final submission of e-Visa application. The applicant would be    responsible for any discrepancy irrespective of grant/rejection of e-Visa application. However, if any discrepancy found on ETA, e-Visa Support Centre may be contacted at indian-evisa[at]gov[dot]in or    (+91) 82 7808 7808 or +91 11 24300666 for assistance at least 24 hours before the journey date. Q31. Is the e-Visa facility allowed for employment Visa? Ans- e-Visa is not allowed for employment. You may apply for a Regular Visa. Q32. Is the e-Visa allowed for Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) activities and journalism purposes ? Ans- e-Visa is not allowed for NGO activities and journalism purposes. However, Voluntary work of short duration (for a maximum period of one month, which do not involve any monetary payment or    consideration of any kind in return) are allowed. Q33. How many attendants can come with a patient? Ans- Only two e-Medical Attendant Visas will be granted against one e-Medical Visa (patient). Am I eligible? You can get a free older person's bus pass if you are: a Southend-on-Sea resident of eligible age. You must check your eligibility date on GOV.UK before applying for a bus pass. We can only accept applications up to 2 weeks in advance of your eligible date or after Supporting documents As part of the online application process, you will have the option to upload: A photo of yourself A recent colour passport style and quality photograph (35mm x 45mm). Please note that hats or sunglasses must not be worn in the photograph. Proof of address Choose 1 of the following or tick the box on the application to confirm we can check your Council Tax records. driving licence utility bill from within the last year bank or credit card statement from within the last year Council Tax bill from within the last year. Proof of identity birth certificate (and marriage certificate if your name has changed) passport driving licence a letter from the pension service confirming you're eligible for the state pension. Once the above have been received, a bus pass will be posted to your address. When and where can I use my bus pass? Find out when and where you can use your bus pass by visiting our using your bus pass page . You cannot use your pass to for free travel on other forms of transport or public transport i.e. tubes, trains, trams, coaches, Dial-a-Ride services, community services and ferries, either within Southend or in other Districts throughout England. The bus pass cannot be used on public services of any kind within Wales and Scotland. Expiry date of passes When your pass expires it will be renewed automatically and you should get your new one before the old one expires. Change of address If you change your address within Southend you need to contact the bus pass department with proof of your new address. Validation of proof of address should be sent to CSCApplications@southend.gov.uk . For proof of address, we can accept one of the following: driving licence utility bill dated within the last 12 months bank or credit card statement dated within the last 12 months Council Tax bill dated within the last 12 months If you move away from Southend you need to return your current pass and re-apply for a new pass from the Authority in the area you are moving to. You can renew your pass, replace a lost or damaged pass, update your details or check your application online, with no need to wait. Log in to your account to get started. We apologise for any delays and thank you for your patience. Close Menu Main navigation Apply for a pass Problem with my pass Pass Information Search Freedom Pass Breadcrumbs Home Apply For a Pass Older Person's Freedom Pass What I Need To Apply What I need to apply Find out what documents and photographs you need before applying for an older person’s Freedom Pass here. Here is what you need to apply for Older Person's Freedom Pass You need 3 things to apply for an older person's Freedom Pass Proof of your name and age Proof of your address and residential status Photograph of yourself If you apply by post, please send photocopies of any documents. Please NEVER send the originals. Original documents will not be returned. 1. Proof of your name and age We require one of the following: Current passport Birth certificate (unless your name has changed) Current driving licence Letter of state pension entitlement (please include your date of birth) European ID card 2. Proof of your address and residential status We require one of the following documents which must be dated within the last 3 months . We advise that you send the most recent document you have. Current council tax bill/letter/payment book Current council/housing association rent book/statement/letter/tenancy agreement Current television licence Residential utility bill/letter (excluding mobile phone bills) dated in the last 3 months HM Revenue and Customs letter dated in the last 3 months Department for Work and Pensions letter dated in the last 3 months Occupational pension letter dated in the last 3 months We do NOT accept: Bank statements Letters from your bank Mobile phone bills If you pay your bills online and do not receive paper copies, a printout of your online bill is acceptable. If you are unable to post or email the required documents, you must contact the Freedom Pass helpline on 0300 330 1433. 3. Photograph All Freedom Pass applications require a passport sized colour photograph taken within the last 12 months. Your photograph must be: Colour and size 45mm x 35mm A current true likeness, showing your full face, facing forward without a hat Taken against a plain, evenly lit and pale coloured background If your photograph does not meet the above requirements we will not be able to accept your application for a Freedom Pass. Need help with the photo? Enter your postcode on Find a photo booth to find your nearest location. How to upload a document to the Freedom Pass application portal Video URL Transcript of video Transcript of video In this example, we show you how to upload evidence of your proof of residency using a council tax bill and a smartphone. You can use the same method when uploading your proof of identification. These instructions are for an Apple iPhone. However, most smartphones and tablets will work in a similar way. You can also use a scanner if you have one, but may need to refer to your scanner's operating instructions. Open the camera function on your phone or tablet and take a picture of your evidence. Make sure that it is a document that we accept, such as for proof of residency, a current council tax bill or utility bill dated within the last 3 months. We must be able to see your name, age, and address details clearly in the pictures. Find the picture you took. Select the icon on the bottom left and then select mail. Type in your email address and press send. You might be asked if you want to add a subject. You can if you want to, but it is not needed. You may also be asked which size you would like to send your image. It is usually best to select small. Go to your computer and log into your emails. Open the email you just sent yourself and click on the image. Download the image and save it onto your computer. In this example, we've saved it onto the desktop. Please note, you will need to save the image in a JPEG, PDF, or TIFF format. If you took the image on your phone or tablet, it will usually be saved as a JPEG automatically. Return to your application form and click choose file. Find where you saved your evidence. Select it by clicking on it once, then click open. You will see a black tick when you have attached it correctly. If you've selected the wrong piece of evidence in error, click delete and start again. If you require further assistance, you can call our helpline or email us. NEXT: Apply for an older person's Freedom pass PREV: Am I eligible?
